items.title: Nobel winner Halzen says years of October 'misery' finally over
items.abstract: Physicist Francis Halzen has an impressively long list of academic accolades—but every October, as the Nobel Prize rolled around, his failure to bag the biggest award of them all left him "miserable," he admits.

items.title: Can a passing black hole disturbance leave a trace in Hawking radiation?
items.abstract: Black holes, despite their extreme nature, are described by surprisingly few basic parameters: their mass, charge and spin. Two black holes may have formed for completely different reasons and passed through very different histories, yet still end up in the same final state. John Wheeler summarized...

items.title: Francis Halzen wins Nobel Prize in physics for work on mysterious ghost particles called neutrinos
items.abstract: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in physics on Tuesday for his efforts to demystify a rare group of neutrinos, tiny cosmic particles that scientists believe offer clues to how the universe evolved.
